sections.brief: Israel's National Health Insurance Law (passed 1994, in force 1 Jan 1995): four funds and shares, health tax 3.2/5.2%, uniform basket, small capped copays, coverage by residence, exclusions (asylum seekers, migrants, foreign workers; Palestinians outside the law), private layer (supplementary ~85–88%), waits; US patchwork (Census 2025: 53.5% employer, 35.8% public, 26.7m/7.9% uninsured), uninsured 2009→2016→2025, enhanced credits expired end-2025, CBO +10m/14.2m by 2034, KFF premiums 2025; aid not in Israel's health budget. Figures: compare

Health spending 2000–2023 on one definition (WHO via World Bank: % GDP and PPP per capita, ratio 3.3x not 'nearly four'); CMS NHE 2024; out-of-pocket share higher in Israel but amount lower; US medical debt (Peterson-KFF SIPP) and the disputed bankruptcy figure (Dobkin/Finkelstein vs Himmelstein/Woolhandler/Warren); drug prices: Israel's reference pricing vs RAND 278%, Medicare negotiation 2026–28 and the 2025 orphan-drug change. Figures: stats; compare

Life expectancy 1980–2024 (level in 1980, ~4-year gap by 2024; CDC 79.0); infant mortality 1980–2024 reversal; modelled maternal mortality; gaps inside each country (Israel MoH Arab/Jewish LE and infant mortality; CDC infant mortality by race); mental health (Israel 2015 reform, waits, post-7 Oct demand and NIS 1.4bn programme; US NSDUH 52.1% treated, suicides 2024); balance of both records. Figures: compare; stats
